heading: The same IOI circuit operates across name orders, templates and additional names
definition: the circuit carries IOI across name orders, templates and more names; it would fail if other prompt formats used different components or heuristics.
summary: The claim that one circuit handles all prompt variants remains contested. Independent studies support reuse of some circuit components across prompt versions in GPT-2 small, but transfer between versions can fail; these failures challenge broader reuse without directly testing the original circuit of attention heads.

suggested_status.by_scale: C for unrestricted cross-variant identity at <1B and 1–10B. Restricted R2 evidence supports GPT-2-small component reuse; Pythia S2-site dependence does not test circuit-component identity across variants. Toy, 10–100B and >100B coverage is absent from versions.V6.studies_by_size.
suggested_status.reason: The broad claim has a credible challenge from bidirectional cross-variant transfer failures on GPT-2 Small and instructed Llama/Qwen edge circuits (arXiv:2605.09129#r4, arXiv:2605.09129#r5, arXiv:2605.09129#r6, arXiv:2605.09129#r7), although the original head circuit is not directly tested. Transfer outcomes require separate condition groups: bidirectional successes support transfer, one-way outcomes limit its scope, and bidirectional failures challenge it (arXiv:2605.09129#r1, arXiv:2605.09129#r2, arXiv:2605.09129#r3). Restricted GPT-2-small component reuse has causal support from positional-component interventions (arXiv:2406.09519#R3, arXiv:2406.09519#R4) and selected-head patching (arXiv:2605.22462#r5, arXiv:2605.22462#r8, arXiv:2605.22462#r9, arXiv:2605.22462#r12). Pythia replacements establish mature S2 residual-state dependence under varied syntax; reuse or identity of particular circuit components was not tested (arXiv:2610.04119#R51, arXiv:2610.04119#R53, arXiv:2610.04119#R55). counts: versions.V6.verdicts.challenges.studies = 1; versions.V6.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0. Scale coverage follows versions.V6.studies_by_size.
suggested_status.open_questions: Would matched causal tests of the fixed original head circuit, adapted edge circuits and within-head features distinguish shared roles from distinct algorithms across the same name-order, wording, label and additional-person variants? Would transfer failures persist across discovery methods and circuit budgets? Does component identity hold for multi-token names and larger scales?

source.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small
source.authors: Kevin Wang; Alexandre Variengien; Arthur Conmy; Buck Shlegeris; Jacob Steinhardt

original_result.setup: Wang et al. tested GPT-2 small's task performance after adding a subject or indirect-object mention, without testing circuit reuse.
original_result.result: An extra subject mention gave a logit difference of 3.64 versus 3.55 at baseline. An extra indirect-object mention reduced it to 1.23, with the subject logit exceeding the indirect-object logit in 23.4% of cases versus 0.7% at baseline.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: The same attention-head classes participated across both name orders.
Rediscovered DoubleIO and TripleIO circuits reused all base nodes and most edges.
The same component carrying position information controlled signal suppression across both name orders.
The same heads retained similar recoveries across vocabulary and cleft-frame changes.
GPT-2 small circuits derived from paraphrases had highly overlapping connections and low error.
The order of interactions between circuit components persisted across wording patterns and name orders.
Mature Pythia models depended on the S2 residual state across varied syntax.
With opening text added, the same pathway carried order information from signal suppression to name copying.
Incidental name duplication preserved near-control accuracy; Duplicate Token and Name Mover heads showed their usual attention patterns.
Backup-head recovery remained similar across alternative IOI templates.
Shared attention-head classes used different rules based on entity properties for different name orders.
The unmodified circuit failed to faithfully reproduce DoubleIO and TripleIO behavior.
The circuit captured BABA behavior more faithfully than ABBA under node mean ablation.
Circuit transfer between IOI variants was usually asymmetric across the tested models.
IOI circuit edges varied across templates despite moderate overlap.
Shared heads used different mechanisms across name orders and wording templates.
Shared heads used different features and slightly different algorithms across name orders.
Incidental repetitions slightly reduced logit differences and shifted some attention in heads that suppress signals.
Circuits failed to transfer both ways: names versus letter labels, and three-person prompts versus filler prompts.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Whether the original fixed 26-head circuit, with its stated roles, carries prompts containing additional distinct people.
untested.basis: arXiv:2605.09129#r5 evaluates three-person variants using newly discovered edge circuits. The original fixed head circuit is not directly evaluated; this gap is inferred from the experimental design, not explicitly stated by the paper. Other studies' untested-parts lines leave additional distinct names untested. counts: versions.V6.coverage_by_operation.evaluation records variant evaluation, but does not establish original-head-circuit coverage.

untested.what: The mechanism supporting multi-token names across prompt variants.
untested.basis: arXiv:2610.04119#R58 reports mature two-token-name behavior only and explicitly says no mechanism was tested. Its untested-parts line leaves multi-token-name mechanisms open; counts: versions.V6.coverage_by_operation.patching does not distinguish such names.

untested.what: Cross-format circuit identity in non-English prompts.
untested.basis: arXiv:2411.16105 reports English prompt templates in Appendix C and no cross-language circuit comparison; the language coverage gap is inferred from study scope, not an explicit untested-languages statement. Its variant evaluations include arXiv:2411.16105#r11 and arXiv:2411.16105#r12. counts: versions.V6.coverage_by_operation contains no language-resolved coverage.

untested.what: Cross-variant mechanism identity at toy, 10–100B and >100B scales, and after fine-tuning or reasoning-specific training.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V6.studies_by_size has entries only for not stated, <1B and 1-10B. versions.V6.studies_by_stage has not stated, base, instruct/chat and other, with no explicit fine-tuned or reasoning category. Mature Pythia checkpoints are covered and are not treated as absent.

untested.what: Whether the same circuit causally carries IOI with incidental modifier-slot IO duplicates, and whether duplicate placement changes its components or heuristics.
untested.basis: lw:zKyKDre78napvtrEo#r1 and lw:zKyKDre78napvtrEo#r4 report logit and attention shifts without causal confirmation of mechanism identity. arXiv:2211.00593#r19 reports degraded behavior with a distractor-sentence IO repetition, whereas lw:zKyKDre78napvtrEo#r2 reports near-control modifier-slot accuracy. These behavioral comparisons do not identify the causal mechanism across placements. counts: versions.V6.coverage_by_operation.evaluation and versions.V6.coverage_by_operation.measurement do not establish this missing causal comparison.

untested.what: Whether recovered backup labels correspond to the same causal name-moving roles and IOI mechanism across the tested handed/passed templates.
untested.basis: arXiv:2607.01940#R20, arXiv:2607.01940#R21 and arXiv:2607.01940#R22 report GPT-2-small (124M) backup-label ROC-AUC of 0.94 on the standard template, 0.93 on alternative template 1 and 0.92 on alternative template 2, using conditional co-ablation after removal of a supplied primary set. These rankings recover fixed labels without testing their name-moving role or circuit behavior on the alternative templates; V6 mechanism identity remains cannot_determine. counts: versions.V6.coverage_by_operation.removal does not distinguish label recovery from functional mechanism comparison.

untested.what: Whether paraphrase-discovered GPT-2-small EAP-IG edge circuits retain the original circuit's head classes, component roles and heuristics, including separately evaluated ABBA/BABA outcomes.
untested.basis: arXiv:2510.00845#R13 reports mean pairwise Jaccard overlap 0.89 (CV 0.10); arXiv:2510.00845#R14 reports mean circuit error 0.01 (CV 0.40) for paraphrase-discovered circuits. Overlap and prediction agreement establish structural stability and functional fidelity of extracted edge circuits, leaving original-circuit mechanism identity cannot_determine. Original head roles and separate name-order outcomes are not checked. counts: versions.V6.coverage_by_operation.measurement does not establish role- or heuristic-level comparison.

untested.what: Whether the same heads, edges and heuristics underlie S2 residual-site dependence across the tested mature Pythia varied-syntax prompts.
untested.basis: arXiv:2610.04119#R51, arXiv:2610.04119#R53 and arXiv:2610.04119#R55 report matched S2 residual-state replacement on 34 varied-syntax prompts at mature Pythia checkpoints: logit-difference changes are −2.150 at 160M, −3.899 at 410M and −1.565 at 1B. These interventions establish site dependence; different components or heuristics could use the same site, leaving V6 circuit identity cannot_determine. counts: versions.V6.coverage_by_operation.patching records Pythia interventions without establishing cross-template head or edge identity.

wording_issues.issue: The evidence spans GPT-2-small heads and features, positional subcomponents, automatically discovered edge circuits, and Pythia residual-stream sites. Shared heads can implement different sJohn/sMary feature mechanisms, challenging V6 at the heuristic level. GPT-2-small paraphrase edge overlap and mature Pythia S2 residual-state dependence under varied syntax leave reuse of the original circuit's head classes, roles and heuristics undetermined. Evidence at these granularities does not establish identity across them.

In GPT-2 small, shared heads use Consecutive Entity features for sJohn and Centered Entity features for sMary; the sJohn mechanism does not work for sMary, challenging V6's heuristic-identity criterion. ACC++ finds ABBA/BABA circuit separation and different incoming signals and upstream heuristics at head (9,9), without measuring order-dependent faithfulness. Separately, node-wise, token-specific mean ablation yields systematically higher BABA than ABBA faithfulness across varying ABC dataset sizes; this demonstrates order sensitivity without establishing different components or heuristics. SAE analysis finds order-dependent feature importance and opposite QK contribution signs within shared heads.

GPT-2-small selected-head patching effects remain similar after content-word replacement and a cleft-frame change. Paraphrased GPT-2-small EAP-IG circuits show high edge overlap, but original head roles and heuristic identity remain undetermined. Pythia-160M routing varies with wording. GPT-2 Small edge circuits fail transfer in both directions between personal names and 'Person X' letter labels, challenging V6 for that pair; the original head circuit is not directly evaluated. These prompt manipulations and mechanistic measurements need to be specified separately.

Additional occurrences of an existing name, additional distinct people, letter labels and multi-token names are different manipulations. GPT-2-small DoubleIO/TripleIO prompts repeat existing IO names. Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct edge circuits fail transfer in both directions between three-person and filler variants, challenging transfer for that pair; the original fixed head circuit is not directly evaluated. Letter labels change naming format. Mature Pythia multi-token-name results establish behavior while leaving the mechanism untested.

Component reuse and heuristic identity give different results in GPT-2 small. Shared heads implement Consecutive Entity features for sJohn and Centered Entity features for sMary; the sJohn mechanism does not work for sMary. This meets V6's explicit different-heuristics failure criterion and challenges the claim despite head reuse. SAE analysis finds order-dependent feature contributions within shared heads, and ACC++ finds different upstream heuristics feeding a shared name-mover head.

method_sensitivity.what: In GPT-2 Small, shared attention heads implement different feature-level mechanisms across name orders. The sJohn order uses Consecutive Entity and Consecutive Entity Association features; sMary uses Centered Entity and Centered Entity Association features. The sJohn mechanism does not work for sMary, challenging V6 at the heuristic level despite head reuse. Attention-output SAE analysis also reports order-specific features and heuristics.

For GPT-2-small IOI, BABA faithfulness is systematically higher than ABBA under node-wise, token-specific mean ablation; ABC replacement-dataset size varies. This shows measured coverage differences, without demonstrating different components or heuristics. For DoubleIO, figure-derived circuit logit differences are 2.485 with IO first and 0.927 with subject first; full-model values are 2.829 and 1.199, respectively. Full-model performance cannot determine V6 mechanism identity. Head 2.2 attention is order-dependent: subject first, IO+1 → IO 0.26 and S+1 → S 0.57; IO first, IO+1 → IO 0.56 and S+1 → S 0.27.
Duplicated-IO variants retain the original nodes but require added IO paths to improve agreement with the full model. Reusing nodes does not imply that the fixed edge structure transfers.
ACC++ circuits organize mainly by name order in GPT-2 small, by wording in Pythia-160M, and less consistently in Gemma-2 2B.

method_sensitivity.factor: Prompt template in per-sample circuit discovery
method_sensitivity.what: GPT-2-small IOI per-sample CEAP circuits of 6000 edges depend on the prompt template across ABBA_00–ABBA_06 and BABA_00–BABA_06. Figure 34 presents the pairwise Jaccard matrix; a numerical cross-template range is not stated. These results concern discovered edge circuits; shared head roles are not compared.

GPT-2-small primary–backup interaction is 1.080 logits under template-conditioned mean ablation and 1.268 under zero ablation. Primary–negative interaction is 1.830 and 1.681 logits, respectively; interaction ordering remains consistent across prompt conditions.

method_sensitivity.factor: Variant pair, transfer direction and model
method_sensitivity.what: Cross-variant edge-circuit transfer depends on its direction and the prompt change. Names versus letter labels fail bidirectionally on the tested models, while broader variant comparisons also show one-direction transfer.
